digest.en: Putin signals readiness for final Ukraine deal talks, shifting focus from a temporary truce. Trump confirms Musk lifted Starlink restrictions on Kyiv after reported operational issues. These moves tighten the diplomatic and technological noose around Moscow.
digest.hi: जर्मनी ने यूरोपीय संघ के कार्बन टैक्स योजना को मंजूरी दी, जिससे इस साल स्टील उद्योग पर 310 अरब यूरो का अतिरिक्त बोझ पड़ेगा।

articles.title: Russia ready for talks on plans for final Ukraine deal, not truce: Putin
articles.summary: Vladimir Putin stated that Russia is prepared to negotiate a final settlement for the Ukraine conflict rather than a temporary ceasefire. The Russian president told state television that discussions should focus on establishing long-term security guarantees for both nations. He explicitly rejected the idea of a short pause in fighting as a sufficient outcome. This position clarifies Moscow's current diplomatic stance on the war's endgame.

articles.title: Women are protesting around Poland for free access to legal abortions
articles.summary: Polish women are protesting across the country to demand free access to legal abortions. The demonstrations target new draft laws that activists argue offer only token gestures rather than genuine reform. Zofia Marcinek of the Abortion Dream Team in Warsaw criticized the timing of the legislation. She noted the bills are being passed a year before the next parliamentary election. Critics view the move as a political maneuver rather than a substantive change to reproductive rights.

articles.title: UN climate damages fund earmarks $20 million to Nepal for August disaster
articles.summary: The UN climate damages fund allocated $20 million to Nepal for August disasters. This marks the first country-specific payout since the fund launched in 2022. The sum covers a small fraction of Nepal's estimated $5 billion loss. Total pledges stand at $820 million against $2.8 billion in requests. This is the first time that the Fund, set up in 2022, has allocated money to a specific country; amount is a fraction of Nepal’s own $5 billion loss estimate; so far, Fund has pledges for $820 million while fielding requests worth $2.8 billion.

articles.title: American detained in Russia arrives in U.S.: lawyer
articles.summary: Stephen Hubbard, an American detained in Russia, has arrived in the United States. His lawyers confirmed his release after a seven-year prison sentence. He was accused of acting as a mercenary for Ukraine. Hubbard was captured in the Ukrainian city of Izium in 2022. Stephen Hubbard’s family and lawyers have said he was living in the Ukrainian city of Izium when he was taken captive by Russia in 2022.

articles.title: Deportations And Jail Terms Leave Tajik Dissidents In Europe Fearing For Their Future
articles.summary: Tajik dissidents report feeling abandoned by Western nations following recent deportations. Several opposition figures were expelled from Germany and other European countries. They face imprisonment upon returning to Tajikistan. Exiled activists now fear losing the diplomatic support they previously relied on for protection. The deportation of several Tajik opposition figures from Germany and other European countries, and their subsequent imprisonment, have heightened fears among Tajik oppositionists in exile.

articles.title: Ukraine Cuts Chinese Drone Dependence, But Critical Gaps Remain
articles.summary: Ukraine has sharply reduced its reliance on Chinese drone components since 2022. However, critical parts remain difficult to replace at scale and cost. This leaves a persistent dependency on Beijing for essential military hardware. In 2022, Ukraine relied almost entirely on Chinese components for its military drones. While that dependency has now been drastically reduced, Ukraine still relies on Beijing for essential parts that remain difficult to replace at the necessary scale and cost.

articles.title: Australia’s NextDC stock collapse fires a global AI warning
articles.summary: Australia’s NextDC stock collapse signals a shift in data center investment. AI’s high computing demands have disrupted the sector’s traditional stability. Investors now face heightened risk as infrastructure costs surge to meet new requirements. For two decades, data centers were relatively safe, lucrative real estate investments. They attracted investors because they served as digital infrastructure. the essential plumbing that keeps the internet running.

articles.title: China’s new drone mothership targets US undersea edge
articles.summary: China built a second drone mothership to launch submarine-sized uncrewed vessels. The platform targets US undersea dominance in the Western Pacific. This capability extends autonomous power beyond the First Island Chain. It systematically challenges American submarine operations in the region. China’s development of specialized naval auxiliaries designed to transport, launch and recover submarine-sized uncrewed vessels signals an assertive push to project autonomous undersea power beyond the First Island Chain and systematically challenge US submarine dominance in the Western Pacific.

articles.title: Don’t mistake Indonesia’s MSCI scare for economic weakness
articles.summary: MSCI proposed downgrading Indonesia to a Standalone Market. Jakarta’s financial community reacted with anxiety and capital flight. Regulators moved to calm investors. The market tremor does not reflect the country’s overall economic health or structural stability. When MSCI floated the idea of downgrading Indonesia to a Standalone Market, anxiety quickly swept through Jakarta’s financial community. Predictably, alarming headlines immediately pointed to foreign capital flight, stock prices dropped and local regulators quickly moved to calm jittery investors.

articles.title: Trump Says Musk Has Lifted Starlink Restrictions On Ukraine After Kyiv Reported Ongoing Issues
articles.summary: Ukraine awaits answers from the Pentagon and SpaceX regarding satellite communication restrictions. Kyiv’s top diplomat in Washington confirmed the lack of clarity. A bipartisan congressional push for an investigation into the restrictions has intensified. Ukraine has yet to receive answers from the Pentagon or Elon Musk's SpaceX over restrictions on satellite communications used by its military, Kyiv's top diplomat in Washington told RFE/RL, as a growing bipartisan push for a congressional investigation intensified.

articles.title: North Korea prepares to restart propaganda loudspeakers as ties sour with South
articles.summary: Kim Yo-jong said propaganda loudspeakers will restart along the entire border within days. She inspected fortifications amid worsening ties with South Korea. The state news agency carried her warning. This marks a significant escalation in inter-Korean tensions. articles.title: American Stephen Hubbard Freed After More Than 4 Years In Russian Custody
articles.summary: Russian authorities released Stephen Hubbard, a 74‑year‑old American, after more than four years in custody. Russia has released 74-year-old US citizen Stephen Hubbard, who had been detained since 2022. He had been sentenced to prison for allegedly acting as a mercenary in Ukraine, charges his family disputed. President Vladimir Putin announced Hubbard’s release during talks with US envoy Steve Witkoff.

articles.title: 'World's Tallest' Dam Takes Shape In Tajikistan
articles.summary: Tajikistan is advancing the Soviet-era Roghun Dam project after securing major funding tranches. The development aims to reshape Central Asia's energy supply. The construction will displace tens of thousands of local villagers from their homes. The Soviet-era Roghun Dam project has endured decades of uncertainty and opposition. Now major funding tranches appear to have the project on track to transform Central Asia's energy landscape -- and displace tens of thousands of Tajik villagers.

articles.title: Taiwan charges five men over plot to run over comedian for his Xi Jinping jokes
articles.summary: New Taipei prosecutors charged five men with plotting to injure comedian Huang Yi-hao. A Chinese national allegedly paid them to ram a car into him. Huang had mocked Xi Jinping and the Chinese Communist party. Person named ‘K’ from China paid five defendants to injure Huang Yi-hao, New Taipei prosecutors sayTaiwanese prosecutors have charged five men over a plot to ram a car into a comedian who made fun of the Chinese Communist party and Xi Jinping. Taiwan has repeatedly accused China of transnational repression to silence critics on the self-governed island, which Beijing claims as its territory and has.

articles.title: When Big Tech becomes a tool of state control in Kenya
articles.summary: Access Now's 2025 report documented 313 global internet shutdowns. Africa saw 30 shutdowns across 15 countries during the period. Protests served as the primary trigger for these outages. Elections followed as the second most common cause for state-imposed connectivity cuts. Access Now's 2025 report found that at least 313 shutdowns were implemented globally, and that in Africa the Internet was shut down 30 times in 15 countries, with protests the leading trigger, followed by elections.

articles.title: Severely ill ICE detainees face imminent deportation to unknown African states, advocates say
articles.summary: Families report ICE is deporting severely ill detainees from Florida jails. Flights to unknown African countries are scheduled for Wednesday. Advocates say the detainees have no ties to these destinations despite worsening medical conditions. Flights to third countries where the detainees have no ties are scheduled as early as Wednesday, relatives detailRelatives of gravely ill detainees at two Florida immigration jails say authorities are about to deport their loved ones to unknown countries in Africa despite worsening medical conditions. Flights are scheduled as early as Wednesday, according to the families and the immigration advocac.

articles.title: Peace efforts resume to end ‘drone war’ fuelling humanitarian crisis
articles.summary: Sudan peace talks resumed in Geneva on Wednesday. Nearly two dozen countries met to discuss a ceasefire. The goal is a transition to peaceful governance that represents all Sudanese people amid the ongoing drone war. Talks to halt the fighting in Sudan and alleviate the humanitarian crisis there continued in Geneva on Wednesday, where nearly two dozen countries convened to discuss a pathway to a ceasefire and transition to peaceful governance that represents all Sudanese people.

articles.title: Global warming will breach 1.5°C – but deep, fast cuts can still bring it back
articles.summary: Global temperatures will exceed 1.5 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. Nations must implement deep, rapid emissions cuts to minimize this overshoot. The goal is returning to the agreed threshold by century's end. Urgent action is required to limit the duration of this breach. With global temperature rise set to exceed 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels, countries “must pull out all the stops” and urgently cut emissions to minimize the overshoot and return to the internationally agreed threshold by the end of this century.

articles.title: Migrants paid up to $500 million in smuggling fees on European sea routes
articles.summary: The UN reported that migrants paid up to 500 million dollars in smuggling fees on European sea routes last year. The figures come from a joint report by UNODC and the International Organization for Migration. The price tag for smuggling on European sea routes reached up to half a billion dollars last year, the UN Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) and the UN migration office, IOM, reported on Wednesday.

articles.title: US Citizen Accused By Moscow Of Fighting For Ukraine Released From Russian Prison
articles.summary: Stephen Hubbard, a 74-year-old retired Michigan teacher, was released from Russian custody. He had been detained since 2022 on charges of joining Ukraine's armed forces. The Kremlin framed his release as a goodwill gesture. His freedom marks a significant shift in the ongoing diplomatic standoff. Stephen Hubbard, a 74-year-old retired teacher from Michigan held by Russia since 2022 on accusations of joining Ukraine's armed forces, has been freed in what is being framed as a goodwill gesture by the Kremlin.

articles.title: Vladimir Putin's Neighbors: Two Parallel Worlds On Lake Valdai
articles.summary: Residents near Lake Valdai in Russia’s Tver region face restricted access to the lake and surrounding forests due to the security perimeter around Vladimir Putin’s residence. The area is fortified with fences, security forces, and air defense systems. Local families bear the economic costs of the war against Ukraine while their recreational access is curtailed. This creates a stark contrast between the protected leadership enclave and the constrained daily lives of nearby citizens.

articles.title: Nigeria confirms Ebola case as outbreak spreads into western Africa
articles.summary: Nigeria confirmed its first Ebola case in Abuja. A woman who traveled from Uganda tested positive after showing symptoms on 7 October. The diagnosis marks the outbreak's spread into West Africa's most populous nation. Case in Africa’s most populous country was detected in a woman who had travelled from UgandaNigeria has confirmed an Ebola case in its capital, Abuja, after a woman who arrived from Uganda tested positive for the virus, the health ministry said. The woman began showing symptoms on 7 October and was admitted to a hospital in Abuja four days later, where she was later diagnosed with Ebola.

articles.title: Wounded Ukrainian Soldier Rescued From Front Lines By Aerial Drone
articles.summary: Ukrainian forces used a hexacopter drone to evacuate a soldier with leg injuries from the front lines. The military described the operation as a first. Fellow servicemen noted the soldier strapped himself to the aircraft and returned to his unit. In what Ukraine's military is calling a historic first, a soldier who suffered injuries to both legs on the battlefield was evacuated by an unmanned aerial drone.

articles.title: Alberta voters overwhelmingly reject plan to leave Canada in referendum
articles.summary: Alberta voters rejected a proposal to begin the independence process by a wide margin. Nearly 1.9 million votes were counted, with 76 percent supporting remaining in Canada. The result delivered a decisive victory for Prime Minister Mark Carney and supporters of Canadian unity. Result is a victory for prime minister Mark Carney and supporters of Canadian unityVoters in Canada’s Alberta have overwhelmingly rejected a proposal to begin the process of independence, delivering a decisive victory for supporters of Canadian unity and deepening divisions within the separatist movement. articles.title: Ukraine Liberates Dnipropetrovsk Settlements, But Villages Lie In Ruins
articles.summary: Ukrainian forces retaken 26 settlements in the Dnipropetrovsk region. The villages are largely destroyed and uninhabitable. Russian troops are being pushed back, but Ukrainian forces face challenges holding the reclaimed territory under constant drone threat. As Russian troops are pushed back, Ukrainian forces face the challenge of holding the reclaimed territory under constant threat from drones. Ukraine Liberates Dnipropetrovsk Settlements, But Villages Lie In Ruins.

articles.summary: जेलेंस्की ने कहा कि पुतिन की गलती से युद्ध लंबा हो गया। उन्होंने बुचा में हुए अत्याचारों का जिक्र किया। जेलेंस्की युद्धविराम और बातचीत के लिए तैयार हैं, लेकिन शर्तें रखी हैं। Russia-Ukraine Peace Talks: यूक्रेन के राष्ट्रपति वोलोदिमिर जेलेंस्की ने साल 2022 से चल रहे रूस-यूक्रेन युद्ध को लेकर एक पॉडकास्ट में बहुत सी बातें बताई हैं। उन्होंने बताया कि रूस के राष्ट्रपति व्लादिमीर पुतिन की ऐसी क्या गलती थी, जिससे तीन दिन में खत्म होने वाला युद्ध आज भी जारी है।

articles.summary: ब्रिस्बेन में 19 वर्षीय युवक ने भारतीय परिवार पर नस्लीय हमला किया और अपार्टमेंट उड़ाने की धमकी दी। पुलिस ने उसे गिरफ्तार किया, परंतु कोर्ट ने सख्त शर्तों पर जमानत दे दी। पीड़ित परिवार भारत लौटने पर विचार कर रहा है। ऑस्ट्रेलिया के ब्रिस्बेन में 19 वर्षीय युवक ने एक भारतीय परिवार पर नस्लीय हमला किया और उनके अपार्टमेंट को उड़ाने की धमकी दी.
